title: Seated Catch-and-Shoot Spots
description: A shooter catches a pass at three spots around the arc and releases immediately from a seated set position, building a repeatable shot that doesn't depend on momentum from the chair.

content.objective: Catch the ball already squared to the basket and release in one smooth motion from the chair.
content.setup: A passer feeds the shooter in turn at the left wing, top of the key and right wing.
instructions: The shooter squares the chair to the basket before the pass arrives.
Catch with the hands already shaped for the shot, no extra adjustment.
Release in one motion using the legs' trunk and shoulders for power, not a stand-up or lean.
Make five at each spot before the passer moves the shooter to the next one.
coachingPoints: Square the chair to the rim before the catch, not after.
Drive the shot with the trunk and shoulders — the power comes from the upper body, not from rocking the chair.
Hold the follow-through after every release.
commonMistakes: Catching off-angle and having to re-square before shooting, which slows the release.
Using the chair's momentum to generate power instead of the upper body.
Dropping the follow-through early instead of holding it.
content.safety: Keep the passer out of the shooter's direct line to the basket.
progressions: Add a defender's hand in the shooter's face without contact once the form is solid.
variations: Move the three spots out to the three-point line for an advanced group.
